senses.definition: (dated) A carnival performer specializing in bizarre and unappetizing behavior.
examples: I once saw a geek bite the head off a live chicken.

quotes.text: You hand in your ticket / And you go watch the geek / Who immediately walks up to you / When he hears you speak / And says, “How does it feel to / be such a freak?”
quotes.reference: 1965, Bob Dylan, “Ballad of a Thin Man”, in Highway 61 Revisited:

senses.definition: (colloquial) A person who is intensely interested in a particular field or hobby and often having limited or nonstandard social skills. Often used with an attributive noun.
examples: I was a complete computer geek in high school, but I get out a lot more now.
Most famous actors are really theater geeks at heart.

senses.definition: (colloquial, by extension) An expert in a technical field, particularly one having to do with computers.
examples: My laptop’s locked up again. I need a geek.

quotes.text: I challenge these geeks to show a little spirit and produce an 81 tier bonfire by Friday night. It would also be nice to see a few kegs and some spirit around their awaited creation each night. Until then I rest my case.
quotes.reference: 1978 November 14, Jeff Boylan, “Excerpts”, in Bob Wasserman, editor, The Tech, volume 98, Cambridge, Massachusetts: MIT, archived from the original on 10 Aug 2014, page 1:

quotes.text: The community of radio amateurs—trespassing fiddlers on the cutting edge of technological possibilities—prefigured the geek community that was to inhabit Silicon Valley 50 years later.

senses.definition: (uncountable, colloquial) The subculture of geeks; an esoteric subject of interest that is marginal to the social mainstream; the philosophy, events, and physical artifacts of geeks; geekness.

quotes.text: It is totally counter-intuitive. How do these ubernerds get the cute girls? Is it the ultimate triumph of the Bill Gates era, in which geek is the new cool?

quotes.text: "Basically," says [Harry J.] Knowles [founder, 'Ain't It Cool News' website], "it's my job to stay on top of the latest and coolest in geek that's out there, specifically as it relates to the world of film."

senses.definition: (colloquial) An unfashionable or socially undesirable person.
examples: Why do you hang around with them? They’re just geeks.
But you can't be any geek off the street, gotta be handy with the steel, if you know what I mean, earn your keep.

quotes.text: Yeah, well, listen. You ought to ditch the two geeks you're in the car with now and get in with us. But that's all right, we'll worry about that later.

senses.definition: (intransitive) To perform bizarre and unpleasant feats as part of a carnival.

quotes.text: Geeking, unsurprisingly, was among the first carnival acts to be outlawed as the 20th century unfurled.

senses.definition: (intransitive, colloquial) To enthusiastically engage in geek-like or nerdy interests.
examples: It was our first time at a Star Trek convention and we had an amazing time wandering around and geeking.

senses.definition: (intransitive, African-American Vernacular, slang) To be nervous or hyperactive due to using crack cocaine.
